hypothesis: H16/H17 raise evidence recall; does that translate into decision accuracy? Score the trained E1 model over dev pairs re-exported with the R2 retriever.
design: Cheap probe, minutes not hours: sextant neural-probe with models/E1/neural over data/neural/bench_dev_r2.jsonl (exported with --local-idf --q-expand) versus the parity export. Train/inference parity is deliberately broken, so the result is directional only: an accuracy GAIN despite the mismatch is strong evidence for the retriever and justifies the full E1b run; a loss is ambiguous and E1b is skipped.

design: Identical to E1 in every hyperparameter, seed and schedule; the ONLY difference is that every pair is exported with --local-idf --q-expand and scorer.json records both flags. Run only if P1 is positive.

hypothesis: H13/H19: a learned linear ranker over the features retrieval already computes beats the pooled BM25 ordering. The gold span is a median 38 words against a 140-word block, so the budget is not the binding constraint, the ranking is: a perfect ranker would retrieve nearly every span where BM25 retrieves 0.31.
design: 16 features per segment (z-scores and rank percentiles of the question / pooled / best-candidate BM25 vectors, question and candidate term coverage, candidate char-4-gram containment, length ratio, document position, focus-field flag, number/date/negation flags, log segment count). Trained listwise: softmax over a state's segments, loss is -log of the mass on the annotated evidence segments. Linear on purpose: it scores every segment of every state on the inference path, so it must cost one dot product. Selected on a held-out slice of the TRAINING pool, never on bench dev or the long-context suite.
data: data/synthetic/bench_train.jsonl + data/synthetic/bench_train_lc.jsonl (the extended long-context training split, 256-16384 tokens)
metric: budget recall at 140 words on held-out train lists for selection; evidence recall on data/bench_internal/long_context.jsonl as the clean headline measurement
notes: R3 and R4 rejected; R8 showed the gain was contiguity, not ranking.

hypothesis: The training pool's long-context curriculum stopped at 1024 tokens while the evaluation suite runs to 16384, so every model had to extrapolate 16x on the axis that already fails hardest. Covering the full range should lift long-context accuracy.
design: data/synthetic/bench_train_lc.jsonl, 3600 records over 256-16384 tokens from the disjoint train-side template pool, verified by scripts/synth/bench/verify.py (every gold re-derived, 0 template overlap, 0 state leakage). Add it to the training files of the next cross-encoder run and compare like for like.

hypothesis: A cross-encoder trained against the improved evidence and the full-length curriculum beats the symbolic champion by a wide margin, especially on long context.
design: Same architecture and hyperparameters as E1 so the comparison to it is clean, with three independently validated changes folded in: R2 retrieval (state-local idf + question expansion, recall 0.288 to 0.306), R8 contiguity (neighbour glue 3, recall 0.306 to 0.462) and C1 curriculum (bench_train_lc.jsonl, 256 to 16384 tokens, closing the gap between a training pool that stopped at 1k and an evaluation suite that runs to 16k). Each was measured on its own metric before being adopted, so folding them together is a change of baseline rather than a confounded experiment; the promotion comparison is against C0. Training sources mirror E1's (the synthetic bench pool plus the real-corpus processed splits) with the C1 long-context split added, so the only differences from E1 are the three intended ones. Also carries the corrected Noul gold convention: E1 was trained with the label pointing at the candidate whose text says the statement does NOT hold, which cost 0.30 of Noul accuracy until the engine was taught to read it back. E5 trains on labels that match their candidate, so it should not need the compatibility flag.
